boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten no-admission, no-purchase ways to spend time with art, civil-rights history, and public exhibits in Atlanta.

cards.title: Browse Cosby Gallery together
cards.subtitle: Spelman College Museum of Fine Art • Camille Olivia Hanks Cosby Academic Center
cards.notes: Meet at the first-floor gallery, take a slow lap through the current exhibition, then trade one artwork each person wants to revisit.
cards.short_summary: A free, public-facing Spelman art stop with a built-in conversation prompt.
cards.evidence_claim: Spelman College Museum of Fine Art states that admission is free and open to the public; Cosby Gallery is on the first floor of the Camille Olivia Hanks Cosby Academic Center.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit | Spelman College Museum of Fine Art
cards.access_notes: Open Wednesday–Saturday, 12–5 p.m.; closed during Spelman College breaks. Check the museum page before going.

cards.title: Walk the Bank of America Gallery
cards.subtitle: Spelman College Museum of Fine Art • CI&A
cards.notes: Use the gallery’s current exhibition as a quick art break: look closely, compare details, and leave time to discuss what caught attention.
cards.short_summary: A free Spelman museum gallery in the Center for Innovation & the Arts.
cards.evidence_claim: Spelman College Museum of Fine Art states that admission is free and open to the public; the Bank of America Gallery is on the first floor of the Mary Schmidt Campbell Center for Innovation and the Arts.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit | Spelman College Museum of Fine Art
cards.access_notes: Open Wednesday–Friday, 1–5 p.m.; closed during Spelman College breaks. Confirm exhibition access before departure.

cards.title: Take in Atlanta Contemporary
cards.subtitle: 535 Means Street NW • Westside
cards.notes: Register for a gallery visit, choose one exhibition to move through slowly, and compare notes outside after your last room.
cards.evidence_claim: Atlanta Contemporary states that admission is always free.
cards.access_notes: The institution asks visitors to register. Check the current exhibition schedule and closure notices before traveling.

cards.title: Pause at the King Crypt
cards.subtitle: The King Center outdoor campus • 449 Auburn Avenue NE
cards.notes: Walk the outdoor campus at an unhurried pace, pause at the crypt, and use the surrounding memorial space for a reflective conversation.
cards.short_summary: A free outdoor memorial stop on The King Center campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The King Center says admission and parking are free and that visitors can view Dr. and Mrs. King’s crypt on its outdoor campus.
cards.access_notes: The King Center lists daily hours of 10 a.m.–5 p.m. and notes holiday closures.

cards.title: See the Eternal Flame
cards.subtitle: The King Center outdoor campus • 449 Auburn Avenue NE
cards.notes: Start at the Eternal Flame, then follow the outdoor campus features in sequence and give everyone time to read and reflect quietly.
cards.short_summary: A no-cost outdoor landmark within the King Center’s public campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The King Center says admission and parking are free and identifies the Eternal Flame among the outdoor-campus features visitors may view.
cards.access_notes: The King Center lists daily hours of 10 a.m.–5 p.m. and notes holiday closures.

cards.title: Walk the Reflecting Pool
cards.subtitle: The King Center outdoor campus • 449 Auburn Avenue NE
cards.notes: Use the pool as the route through the campus: walk its length, notice the memorial elements, and pause before heading into Freedom Hall.
cards.short_summary: A free outdoor walk linking major King Center memorial features.
cards.evidence_claim: The King Center says admission and parking are free and directs visitors to walk east along the Reflecting Pool on its outdoor campus.
cards.access_notes: The King Center lists daily hours of 10 a.m.–5 p.m. and notes holiday closures.

cards.title: Explore Freedom Hall exhibits
cards.subtitle: The King Center • 449 Auburn Avenue NE
cards.notes: Continue from the Reflecting Pool into Freedom Hall and spend time with the exhibits before comparing one takeaway from the visit.
cards.short_summary: Free King Center exhibits for a focused indoor history stop.
cards.evidence_claim: The King Center says admission and parking are free and describes Freedom Hall as a place to learn through its exhibits about Dr. King, Mrs. King, and The King Center.
cards.access_notes: The King Center lists daily hours of 10 a.m.–5 p.m. and notes holiday closures.

cards.entity_name: Martin Luther King, Jr. National Historical Park Visitor Center
cards.title: See the park’s visitor-center exhibits
cards.subtitle: Martin Luther King, Jr. National Historical Park • Sweet Auburn
cards.notes: Begin at the temporary visitor center for orientation, then explore the featured exhibits and make a plan for the rest of the historic district.
cards.short_summary: A fee-free National Park Service exhibit stop in the Sweet Auburn district.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service says Martin Luther King, Jr. National Historical Park is fee-free year-round with no entrance fee or pass required, and its visitor center offers featured exhibits.
cards.source_title: Basic Information | Martin Luther King, Jr. National Historical Park
cards.access_notes: NPS lists the visitor-center facilities as open daily, 9 a.m.–5 p.m.; the visitor center is temporarily at Fire Station No. 6 during renovations.

cards.entity_name: Historic Ebenezer Baptist Church Church Talk
cards.title: Join a Historic Ebenezer Church Talk
cards.subtitle: Martin Luther King, Jr. National Historical Park • Sweet Auburn
cards.notes: Check the park calendar, arrive early for the day’s church talk, and leave room afterward to walk the surrounding historic district.
cards.short_summary: A free ranger-led interpretation at Historic Ebenezer Baptist Church.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service states that Historic Ebenezer Baptist Church Church Talks are conducted daily, and that Martin Luther King, Jr. National Historical Park is fee-free year-round.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit | Martin Luther King, Jr. National Historical Park
cards.access_notes: Church-talk times are listed on the park calendar. NPS lists park hours as daily, 9 a.m.–5 p.m.; verify same-day details.

cards.entity_name: Dr. King Birth Home Ranger Presentation
cards.title: Ask about a Birth Home presentation
cards.subtitle: Martin Luther King, Jr. National Historical Park • Sweet Auburn
cards.notes: Check in at the visitor center on arrival and ask about presentation availability; plan another nearby park stop in case capacity is filled.
cards.short_summary: A free ranger-led presentation at the home where Dr. King was born.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service says ranger-led Birth Home presentations are offered daily free of charge, are limited to 15 people, and are first come, first served.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit | Martin Luther King, Jr. National Historical Park
cards.access_notes: Presentations are capacity-limited and first come, first served; consult the park calendar and ask at the visitor center upon arrival.
